reference.source: Parsons' Diseases of the Eye 23rd Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
reference.pathophysiology: Glycosaminoglycan deposition expands orbital fat and muscle bellies within a rigid bony box, raising intraorbital pressure toward the apex where the optic nerve strangulates; valveless ophthalmic veins conduct sinus infection posteriorly to both cavernous sinuses.
additionalDifferentials: Preseptal versus orbital cellulitis by globe and vision
Thyroid myopathy versus myasthenia by fatigability and antibodies
Cellulitis versus pseudotumour by fever and sinus disease
additionalInvestigations: Contrast CT or MRI orbit with sinuses and apex
Thyroid function, counts, and lesion biopsy
